sections.heading: Waiting for you with my heart turned toward you
sections.text: Most High God, I am here because you have called me to seek you. I am waiting for you in the path you have given me, not trying to force my own way. I want your name to matter to me more than anything else, and I want my mind to keep returning to you instead of drifting away.

scripture_references.connection: This passage speaks of waiting for the Lord in the way he has appointed, with desire directed toward his name and remembrance. It closely grounds the opening movement of the prayer.
The psalm calls God's people to wait for the Lord with courage and dependence, which supports the prayer's posture of patient trust rather than self-directed striving.

sections.heading: Coming to you honestly as a sinner who still has hope
sections.text: I am a sinner, and I do not want to be numb to that. My sins are many, and they are worse than I often admit. But you are not small in mercy. You have more than enough grace for me. The blood of your Son can cleanse me completely, and your Spirit can bring even my strongest sinful desires under your rule.

scripture_references.connection: John holds together honest confession and real cleansing through the blood of Jesus. This supports the prayer's confidence that great sin is not greater than God's provision in Christ.
Paul teaches that believers put sinful deeds to death by the Spirit. This grounds the prayer's request that the Spirit subdue even powerful, stubborn desires.

sections.heading: Asking for a conscience that will not make peace with sin
sections.text: Give me a conscience that stays tender and awake. When I sin, do not let me shrug it off or explain it away. Let conviction hurt enough to bring me back to you quickly. Make me the same person when no one sees me as when people are watching, the same in comfort as in trouble. Teach me to receive all your commands as good and right, and to reject every path that leads away from you.
theological_themes: Integrity in private and public life

scripture_references.connection: David asks God to search him and expose any grievous way in him, so that he may be led in God's way. This supports the desire for a conscience that welcomes God's searching work.
Paul describes his aim to keep a clear conscience before God and people. That fits the prayer's concern for integrity in both hidden life and outward conduct.
The psalmist affirms God's precepts as right and rejects false ways. This grounds the prayer's request to love God's commands without selective obedience.

sections.heading: Refusing to settle where I am
sections.text: Do not let me become satisfied with where I am spiritually. Keep me growing. Add to my faith the strength to do what is right, a deeper knowledge of you, self-control, steady devotion, kindness toward other believers, and real love. Help me not to neglect anything that belongs to a mature Christian life.
theological_themes: Faith expressed in virtue and love

scripture_references.connection: Peter calls believers to supplement faith with virtue, knowledge, self-control, godliness, brotherly affection, and love. This is the direct biblical pattern behind this section's desire for spiritual growth.
Paul refuses to speak as though he has already arrived, but presses on toward Christ's call. This supports the prayer's rejection of spiritual complacency.

sections.heading: Making the gospel visible in ordinary life
sections.text: Shape what is useful in me. Grow what is beautiful in your sight. Let my life make the gospel look true and good, not cheap or empty. May the way I speak, work, suffer, serve, and respond to circumstances point people toward Jesus. Help me receive your providence with trust and adjust faithfully to what you put in front of me.

scripture_references.connection: Paul teaches that ordinary conduct can adorn the doctrine of God our Savior. This supports the prayer's desire that a believer's life make the gospel attractive and credible.
Paul calls Christians to do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus. This grounds the prayer's desire for faithfulness in speech, work, service, and everyday responsibilities.

sections.heading: Keeping your truth close for the hard day
sections.text: When a dark or evil day comes, keep me from collapsing under it, and keep me from sinning in response to it. Help me carry your truth into ordinary life, not just store it away for religious moments. Let your teaching shape how I think, your warnings make me careful, your commands guide my choices, and your promises comfort me when I need strength.
theological_themes: Warnings, commands, and promises as means of grace
Dependence on God in temptation and hardship

scripture_references.connection: Paul tells believers to take up God's armor so they can stand in the evil day. This supports the prayer's request not to sink or sin when pressure comes.
The psalmist stores up God's word in his heart so that he will not sin against God. This supports the prayer's desire to carry divine truth into real situations where obedience is tested.
Paul says Scripture was written for instruction, endurance, encouragement, and hope. This fits the prayer's desire for doctrine, warnings, rules, and promises to actively sustain daily life.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original asks for a conscience that can 'smite and torment' the believer when sinning. In contemporary language, that could be confused with spiritual despair or unhealthy scrupulosity, so it has been rendered as painful conviction that leads back to God rather than self-punishment.

The phrase 'accommodate myself to thy providence' can be misunderstood as passive resignation to circumstances. The adaptation keeps the older providential trust but frames it as faithful, trusting responsiveness to what God gives.
significant_interpretive_choices: 'Conversation and conduct' was interpreted in the older sense of one's whole manner of life, including speech, behavior, public consistency, and private integrity.

The list 'faith, virtue, knowledge, temperance, godliness, brotherly kindness, charity' was treated as an intentional echo of 2 Peter 1:5-7 and rendered in contemporary terms while preserving the sequence and substance.

'Cultivate the expedient, develop the lovely, adorn the gospel, recommend the religion of Jesus' was interpreted as a prayer for visible Christian character that serves others and makes the gospel commendable in ordinary life.
